reviews.text: I’ve visited the Great Wall at Badaling a few times, and each visit has its own rhythm. No matter how familiar the place becomes, the first sight of the Wall stretching across the mountains still feels powerful. The scale, the stonework, the way it rises and falls with the ridges — it’s a reminder of just how much history sits in these hills. Badaling is the most visited section, and you feel that energy right away. The crowds can be intense, especially near the main entrances, cable car stations, and the first towers. But once you climb a little higher, the noise fades and the views open up. The mountains around Yanqing are beautiful, and on a clear day the scenery is spectacular — layers of ridges, watchtowers in the distance, and the Wall winding like a ribbon across the landscape. The steps are famously steep in places, something every visitor seems to mention, and each climb feels like a small accomplishment. The cable car and funicular make access easier, especially if you want to start higher and walk down, which many reviewers recommend for a quieter experience. Across multiple visits, what stays with me is the contrast: the lively crowds at the base, the calm stretches higher up, and the sense of standing on something that has watched centuries pass. Even after a few trips, Badaling still offers moments that feel fresh — a new angle of the mountains, a quieter tower, or simply the feeling of being part of a place so much larger than yourself.

On a company business trip to China, I was fortunate enough to have the opportunity to visit the Great Wall, and it was a once-in-a-lifetime experience! I love hiking, and this was a great challenge. The views are spectacular, and I recommend getting an audio guide experience before ascending the wall. You'll get an in-ear history lesson on the whole wall, and on the Badaling site in particular. We spent about 90 minutes hiking up the wall, and there was farther for us to go if we wanted. I'd recommend around 2 hours for hiking. Buy tickets beforehand. Bring comfortable hiking shoes, and don't bring a heavy bag! Your legs WILL get a workout! There is a cable trolly if you want a fast and easy way up or down. In the parking lot, before taking the bus up to the wall, you'll probably be solicited by people selling hats and gloves to keep you warm, and when leaving you'll be solicited again by drivers trying to give you a lift down to the parking lot.

Absolutely brilliant!!!!! We collected tickets at the entrance, no problems, made our own way there. But had to taxi back as a lot of the train times back were fully booked so I recommend having the train booked or just get a taxi. Taxi cost us 40 for a 2 hr taxi home inc tolls. Which we were delighted with as we were recked. Defo worth a visit!!!! 20/10.

Quite a fun experience. Quite easy access by car or high speed rail. The station is just at the foot of the cable car station. Price of cable car about RMB140 and entrance ticket price RMB40 is separate and buy at different windows. Also better go toilet before you take the cable car as it’s not easy to find toilet on the Great Wall. Cable car ride up was smooth and no Q on a Saturday 8am. But tour groups started to form shortly after. Very cold up there on end of October day. Better be dressed for the weather. Nothing much to do up there. Just walk about take pictures. But at least some English descriptions on the building information. You can walk up and down the Great Wall sections. As the morning grew on more and more people filled the area. By the time we left about 11 am the cable car line was very long. You can then go to the shopping street at the base for some food, souvenirs and drinks. Many local and international brands available but unfortunately no toilets in the shops. It’s a centralized toilet concept.

It wasn’t difficult to walk actually. Of course some of the steps are irregular and sloppy. But since it was winter, a lot of people just went there not property geared, so almost slipped and wearing too thick. Was an off peak, but yet humans too many, pictures always full of heads. 😅 Overall, is not a tough one, I thought how hard it was but if you have been hiking and fit, is easy walk. On purpose wanted to take the picture of what was written as 不到长城非好汉。But the original one has moved. They have another one on the other side of the walls, so I went to the other side, more adventurous as it is much tougher and sloppy. But overall, if you are properly gear and well gripped shoes, no worries. There are two of the stone tablets, one is just at the entrance. Go for the higher ones since already here. Less people compared to the side where the original tablet (removed) was.

The Badaling section, 60 km northwest of Beijing in the Yan Mountains, was built mainly during the Ming Dynasty (1368–1644) to defend against Mongol invasions. Its name means "welcoming the masses," reflecting its strategic pass control. Foundations date to the Northern Wei Dynasty (386–534 AD), with the 12-km Ming stretch featuring watchtowers and battlements for patrols and signals. As part of the 21,000-km UNESCO-listed wall from the 7th century BC, it protected Han culture. Opened to the public in 1957 after restoration. The site includes steep inclines, parapets, and beacon towers with ancient inscriptions, offering views of peaks that highlight its hand-built engineering. - Visit in spring (April–May) or autumn (September–October) for mild weather; arrive at opening (6:30–8:00 AM) or after 3:30 PM to avoid crowds. Choose weekdays; book tickets online for holidays. - Wear sturdy hiking shoes with good grip, layer clothing, and carry 1L water, snacks, sunscreen, and hat per person. - Follow the 1.5-km North Line loop from North Eight Tower for balanced challenge; use cable car (¥100–140) if needed. Pace with breaks every 20 minutes. - From Beijing, take S2 train (1 hour, ¥6–40) or 877 bus (90 minutes, ¥12). Entry: ¥40–45; add ¥100 for museum. - Stay on paths, avoid littering; hire guide (¥200–300/hour) for history details. Plan time for post-visit recovery.

Badaling. The Great Wall’s most visited, least enjoyable section — a living monument to the human ability to queue for absolutely everything. First, you queue for the ticket. Then, surprise! You need a shuttle to reach the entrance. Queue again. Once you finally board, you think, “At last, the Wall!” Nope. Another queue for the cable car. And when you get off? Congratulations — you’ve unlocked the main queue, the one on the Wall itself. Walking here feels like competing in the world championship of waiting. You move five steps, stop, and stare at a thousand peace signs and matching tour hats. The view is stunning, but you’ll barely see it through the forest of selfie sticks. The Wall deserves respect. Badaling deserves a traffic management plan and maybe an exorcism. Avoid it unless you really enjoy paying to stand in a human snake made of tourists.

One of China's most noteworthy tourist attractions, considered one of the wonders of the world. If you plan to visit the Badaling Great Wall during winter, be sure to pack clothing, gloves, and a head covering, as the winds are relatively strong on the Great Wall. It offers beautiful views. Enjoy your vacation. I hope you enjoy it...

reviews.text: Checked out the great wall during a 24h layover in China, it is very accessible from the Beijing Capital International Airport (roughly 30 minutes by train, or roughly 1h by buss or taxi) China offers visa-free entry if your visit is 24h or less, be prepaid to fill out a form and provide biometrics (face scan and fingerprints) prior to entering the country The Chinese metro is easy to use and you can buy tickets using regular visa debit (or credit) cards and the tickets are extremely cheap (roughly 0.5 $/€/£), the train is a bit more expensive, but still less than (roughly 2-3$/€/£) Be prepared to show your passport anytime you buy a ticket for something at a payment desk, but everything is otherwise very cheap I would strongly recommend buying an esim, as any Google services are otherwise disabled within the country, and Google maps does not work either (does not provide any navigation in regards to methods of transfer other than car) The alternative navigation apps are either entirely in Chinese or a bit janky, but I would recommend getting Amap (it's in English, and shows exactly where to go using public transport, however be advised that it can still show results for routes that aren't available at the time that you search for them when it comes to buses) Most touristy places allow you to buy using ordinary visa payment, but be advised that the majority of the country uses WeChat and Alipay, which are easy enough to get Worst case, taxi drivers can actually accept USD, and will even be nice enough as to give you change in CNY The wall itself is a pretty magnificent sight to behold and it is pretty fun that you can actually visit it if your flight has a layover, would strongly recommend going if you have the chance
Great experience my kids with us so we didn’t take a long walk, you have to be careful with the steps the cable car cost 400 for each one and the entrance costs 40 but it’s free for the kids

It's not a lot people I recommend visiting this place in the evening. Climb up to the end of the cable car and walk down the wall, it's very quick, takes less than an hour. There won't be too many people at the top and you'll be able to enjoy the view.
Great section of the wall to visit. Got to visit here for free as part of the free trip.com PEK layover transit tour and I highly recommend. Beautiful views and great exercise.
Climbed the Great Wall the hard way—on my legs. Earned the views. Took the cable down and just soaked it all in. Unreal experience.

been here in november, my soul was freezing cold, luckily i bought a scarf after exiting the train station, overall id say this was a marvelous experience, in both the view, and the feeling; side note: it's way more crowded than you think

The most touristic area of Great Wall. It has two sections where you can explore - The right side is the most crowded and scenic. You can go down by a Toboggan ride and you’ll reach the Panda Zoo. The left side is so serene and a little bit peaceful to explore.

As one of the greatest wonders, you must visit it. Wall itself with surrounding is good. We found less visitors during our visit. Better to plan by tour package otherwise difficult to get bus when returning

Loved it, but understandably very crowded. Takes about 2 hours from Beijing with Didi and free shuttle bus to reach the cable car station. Lots of people took food along as it takes a while to get around the wall.

n A Nutshell: -The Great Wall of China at the Badaling section is nice. -You can take the high-speed rail here from Beijing in about 30 minutes. -I liked the restaurant options they had before you enter. -The biggest downside about coming here is the amount of people especially on a hot day. -The upside about coming here is the breeze which helps keep you cool as you traverse along the steep sections of the wall. -You can find some shade w/ cool wind in the sections that are enclosed. Overall, visiting one of the new 7 wonders of the world was another check of the bucket list of life!

Been waiting a long time to come here. Definitely worth the wait to plan and finally check this place out. The hikes are steep so where shoes that have grip to them and be ready for the crowds at the beginning because they're ruthless. I'd recommend this to people who love hiking or just walking. If you crippled or have no stamina, do the rest of us a favor and stay away.
Amazing!! We went on a Monday, with traffic it took over an hour to get here from the city. There were a lot people, we took the cable car it’s 140 yuan. We walked up to the 8th tower very steep.
The Great Wall of Badaling is an incredible experience. I went in early December and the crowds were low with plenty of opportunities for photos and contemplation.

A must visit historical spot for every tourist to Beijing. We planned the visit during the off peak season, thus everything was smooth and easy. Taking the car from Beijing to the Badaling took us about 90 minutes, it all depends on the traffic condition. Although it is during winter, we were so lucky to have sunny weather. For visitors with elderly and kids, or health disabilities, it is advised to take the cable car. There is still a short climb to the peak of Badaling Great wall but it was manageable for most healthy people. It is a very steep climb. It is very crowded at the peak, but worth it to pay a visit. You can have a nice view of the surrounding and see the Great wall extend far into the mountainous area. It is a magnificent view and touched to realize that the ancient Chinese spent thousands of years building this wall preventing the intruder from the north. The best photo spot isn't at the peak but a trench of a great wall nearby. It has a great view under the morning sun. Taking the cable car will help to save you a lot of time and you will be able to complete the visit to the top within an hour or less. But if you would like to enjoy the full experience of Great wall climb, I believe you can enjoy more on foot.

I recently visited the Badaling section of the Great Wall of China, and it was truly an amazing experience. The views of the mountains are breathtaking, and seeing the wall built with limited technology on such rugged terrain changes your entire perspective. It's mind-blowing. The area is very well-maintained and clean. Although we visited on a weekend and it was quite crowded, the experience was still enjoyable. The souvenir shops and restaurants were nice, you have a lot of options to choose from. Navigating the area was relatively easy thanks to good signage, but I recommend doing some research before you go. Be prepared to walk a lot and tackle some seriously steep stairs. Overall, every part of the visit was memorable. Highly recommended for anyone visiting Beijing.

VERY CROWDED Entrance to the Great Wall but still worth it because you can take the bullet train to this entrance and avoid hiring a private driver. After you get through the main area of the crowd, you can continue walking down about 15 minutes and the crowds will start to thin out. This entrance has the Telerik and the toboggan slide (recommended if you bring your kids). You should plan to stay here for 5 hours because there's a lot of walking and you can take a lot of breaks. You'll want to see different areas of the wall.

The easy way to visit Great Wall is by Ropeway, just bought a ticket online with rope car and entry ticket separately, follow the instructions, and do not enter from the public bus entrance, trust me. I took a train from Malaysia to Europe. Beijing was a transit city in my itinerary. Welcome to follow my YouTube channel [Lonely Railway Explorer] and go through my Malaysia to Europe series to know more this attraction and the route I took. Everyone know, Great Wall are must visit attraction in LIFE, and I must say not easy to claim, even I took by rope way reaching at 8 floor, but still far to go. Even down hill also not easy, but everything are worthy after visit. Please take the High-Speed train to Badaling, and change the Ropeway, return you can choose by Public Bus or High-Speed train too. Please watch my YouTube video to know more about the route.

Undoubtedly it is justifying the name, even today. The beauty of the structure, it's planning and execution will teach you the vision of ancient kings. Although it was made for protection but the mesmerizing view from above will make you feel you are in the top of the world. Not all part of the wall is open for visitors. Many day trip package is available form Beijing which can be found in social media.

Badaling is the closest section of the Great Wall to the city area. You’ll often see many students on day trips visiting this part of the wall. Upon exiting the car park, the left side of the wall is steeper, while the right side has a gentler incline, making it easier to climb. Between the wall sections, there is a watchtower that was historically used by guards for night watch duties. The view is impressive, though not as scenic as other sections like Mutianyu and Simatai, which offer better vistas but are less well-maintained compared to Badaling.
The easiest section of the great wall to visit with it's own high speed rail station.

Great Wall of Badaling is accessible by high speed rail, Badaling Great Wall Station and the cable car station is located within few minutes' walk from the high-speed rail station. The Great Wall is an engineering marvel that has withstood centuries of exposure to elements. This is a tourist hotspot where tens of thousands of visitors scale the steep steps to reach the top. Some parts of the wall were closed for restoration work during the visit.

It might not be easy to find out how to visit the Great Wall, but it is actually very easy. You can book the train from Beijing to Badaling at a very cheap rate and then just pay for the entry ticket. Recommended to book everything beforehand on Trip.com, it is very convenient. We were extremely unlucky as there was thick fog the whole time and we could not see anything. Still beautiful!
Suggest to start early as it will be crowded later. Wait time for cable car. Next views and must visit.

Visited as part of a tour, had 2 hrs to explore this section which was enough. It's very steep in places, steps are all different heights. If you go to the top you can come back down the next section and walk back to the car park but this may take about 90 mins, although the second section ( way back down) will be much less crowded Great views, coffee beer and souvenirs available in the car park area. Toilets everywhere, and a cat at the top

Despite the huge crowd and the long lines, I felt grateful I got to see the Great Wall of China...how well they built it and preserved it. I enjoyed the landscapes and he mountain scenery! The people were generally friendly, too.

One of the best experience to witness one side of The Great Wall of China. Superb ancient site the showcase the rich culture of the Chinese Ancient Dynasty. Next time I will visit the other part of the Great Wall. A must experience to do while in Beijing.

The most visited place, but I don’t recommend Badaling side. It was second visit to great wall and I am strongly recommended that if you can take mutianyu great wall visit. It is recommended that take taboggan for return. Generally local tourists visiting this side of Great Wall.

Went on Monday, so many people during 11:00-14:00. I recommend buying a cable car to get up at station 8 then walk down to station 1 (overall around 2 hours). There are some spots where you can enjoy scenery but mostly full of people.

Visiting the Badaling Great Wall of China is a truly remarkable experience. The Badaling section is one of the most well-preserved and iconic parts of the Great Wall. When you visit, you'll be able to marvel at the grandeur and historical significance of this ancient structure. The views from the wall are breathtaking, offering a glimpse into China's rich history and stunning landscapes. It's a must-visit destination for anyone exploring China! *Tips-When visiting the Badaling Great Wall, it's a good idea to arrive early to avoid the crowds and make the most of your time there. Wear comfortable shoes because there are some steep sections and stairs to climb. Don't forget to bring water and snacks, as there are limited options available on the wall itself. 🏯 *Peak visiting times-The peak visiting times at the Badaling Great Wall are usually during weekends and Chinese public holidays. It tends to get crowded during these times, so if you prefer a quieter experience, visiting on weekdays or during the early morning hours is advisable.
Lots of walking needed but there is a rail seat to get you much closer. Needs to be on your bucket list!

A must visit for any tourist in China, it is one of the marvelous feat of the mankind. It really is so wonderful and splendid. And since I went in the final week of December, it was freezing cold with gusty winds. So if you’re going during the winter months, make sure you’re well prepared with warm clothes, cap, gloves and good shoes. There are various points from where you can ascend the Great Wall and badaling was one of the best as I heard.

If you have the opportunity to ever visit the Great Wall of China, do it. Stunning views and so much interesting history. Take water when you go out and walk far though. It is very steep and up and down, I ran it but it was very rough.

Easily came here from Beijing by train. All tickets you should buy in advance . Prepare with you a lot of water and food. Only 1 small shop there . Also you can take swing to go up and down . It was very interesting to climb up

This 2000 plus year old world heritage sight leaves you wondering how this mighty wall was built so long ago. It’s one thing to see the wall in pictures or videos, but it’s a completely different feeling when you’re standing on history itself. It’s not an easy climb with super steep slopes and staircases. For those who don’t want to start from the beginning of the wall, you can choose to take the cable car up to the middle of the wall and continue making your way up or back down the hill. Going down the wall, there’s the choice to take the somewhat old but very fun toboggan ride!

Update Oct. 22nd, 2024: After going to Mu Tian Yu Great Wall area, one thing I’d like to mention is that the Great Wall of Badaling is more reasonably priced in entrance tickets! My American friends are both over 80 and despite of being none Chinese, Badaling ticketing booth still waived them of the entrance tickets! (Their policy is that anyone above age 60 would be waived tickets!). Whereas Mu Tian Yu Great Wall area doesn’t do that to Non-Chinese citizens… Absolutely amazing to re-visit the most famous great wall together with my American friends in their 80’s! I was a teenager last time when I was walking up this part of the Great Wall together with my parents… It was almost 100 degree Fahrenheit, but we loved walking up the steps. So many Chinese - my country peers were friendly with us and even tried to help out my senior friends by offering them umbrella or water, etc. 65 years up seniors are waived with entrance tickets, regardless of nationalities. Imagine it’s 8k kilometers long, and after 2hrs of walking, we only ended up only finished 1.5km of distance! No wonder this is one of the world’s 7 wonders! 👍 👍

reviews.text: We went by the high speed train, only 40 minutes from Beijingbei railway station. From the train station, turn right to the cable car (140 RMB rt or 100 RMB single) or turn left to find the great wall entrance if you wanna walk up. Admission to the wall is 40 RMB.
A very popular but crowded historic place. Yet a must to visit. Take advantage of the cable car.

A must visit 7 wonder that i want to visit since many years ago. Iam glad to pay a visit here with my wife. Great architecture and wisdom of ancient people. Everything is perfect, BUT. The worst thing is still the quality of the people. The whole place mentioned no graffiti and sculpture so mean it allow them to shout, throw rubbish and non stop spitting along the way… the sound is too disgusting and they just spit every where. Really really memorable. Oh ya, pushing you and cutting queue is normal also.

We were there before sunrise on a 1st of January. If you are lucky and early rise, you may have a couple of hours to enjoy the beautiful sight. But once the tour bus start pouring their crowd, you will not even see your feet. The path become as packed as Tokyo subway during rush hours. So go early and enjoy from 5 to 7am. You will need to hire a car to be there early. It is not very far from the City center.

Badaling is well developed for tourists. You may take any of the convenient transportations like high speed rail, train or tour bus from city. Pay extra at entrance for cable car to get up to the Great Wall platform #4, west side to stations # 2 & #3 gives you a flavor of hiking; east side to stations #7 are flat, easy walks.

Breathtaking! A must-see at least once in a life time. In my opinion, the condition is still so hard to climb nowadays, let alone climb hundreds of years ago. You can take the cable car to North 7 Building and walk to “HaoHanPo” at North 8 Building. However, the famous Stone Tablet is not located at the North 8 Building anymore, they moved it to the South 1 Building. (There is another one at the South 4 Building).
Is a good experience to visit the Great Wall of China. Although is cold, but crowd is good, not too many people since it is still not school holiday in China. So mid November is a good time to visit
Recommend taking the cable car uphill and walking downhill. Taling the high-speed train from beijing is the best option to reach here

Definitely one of the must visit attractions if u visit Beijing. Quite crowded on a Sunday and I spent more than 40+mins just waiting for shuttle to the cable car station where u wait another 15+mins. Would recommend taking the cable car up if u did not come in the morning else will take u hrs to climb the steep walls. If u dun like crowds, better come over during weekdays or choose Mutianyu walls instead.

Visiting the Great Wall of China is a once-in-a-lifetime experience. Our visit on February 29th, 2024, took place amidst extremely cold temperatures, around minus 10 degrees, accompanied by strong winds. We accessed the vicinity of the wall via train and cable car. The wall itself is a testament to centuries of hard work, artistry, and stunning beauty. It's truly awe-inspiring to contemplate the level of architectural ingenuity required to construct such a marvel at such a height. I strongly recommend that everyone take the opportunity to witness the historic and grandeur of the Great Wall of China firsthand.
Great to visit, tourist friendly. Large parking available. Please order tickets in advance for the cable cart. We went in June and it was quite busy.

Amazing sight to see but be prepared to ascend and descend very steep steps and slopes, but it’ll be all worth it. “Highly recommend to bring your own water and food as it costs 3x the usual price”. We traveled there on Monday and it was packed with people so I cannot imagine how it is on the weekends. If you want some good photos you will need to walk a fair bit as the area around the entrance is always full of people and the people will constantly walk through and get into your photos. Travelled there with a tour group where they organised my entry ticket (ID required to enter). 140rmb/pp for return tickets on the Gondola and 130rmb/pp for the bus (Pick up from accommodation + bus to Great Wall, Summer Palace & Olympic Park)

I visited the place in October 2023, with amazing views and a few tourists. I took the subway from Lama temple station to Jishuitan station and followed the signs to bus 877 that took me to the main entrance in Badaling. The bus is 12 yuan one way with cash and 6 with Alipay. I walked 15-20 minutes from the entrance and followed the sign for funicular, not the cable car( most tourists go up with the cable car and that section is packed). There was no line, they accepted all kinds of payments, passport required, 140 yuan both ways for funicular and 40 yuan for entrance. When you get up walk first to the right up to the seventh tower where the wall ends for tourists. Then walk back as much as you want, This section was not touristy at all, I have pictures that just 3 tourists are on the long stretch of the wall😊

I have heard about the Great Wall my entire life but even after everything I had heard, it could not have prepared me for the greatness of this place. It felt humbling to walk the stairs and take in the view from the watchtowers. Though I knew it was the longest wall in the world, I was still in awe to see that it stretched as far as the eye can see in both directions! This was a once in a lifetime trip and I would not trade it for anything and neither should you if you ever have the opportunity. The do have small giftshops before you start walking up the steps but I highly recommend waiting until you done to buy anything as there are far more steps then it looks and you do not want to add an weight to your pockets.

Visited many times, this is wonder of the world. The first ever visit was make in 2015, later visited in 2016, 2017, & 2018. It's entrance has significantly changed, there are a variety of facilities nowadays. You can have chopper view. I heard now we can have sky diving there it's really amazing. I highly recommend to visit if you plan to visit Beijing.

I get to Badaling by highspeed train. Indeed, this solution is very conveninent. Only 20_30 minutes by train from Beijing North train station or from Qinghe Train station (but you have to come to Train station to buy ticket directly, no only purchase. You should buy a little bit in advance to secure your seat cause many tourists). When you get our of Badaling station, you see a parking for big buses along a hill. Up of Hill is Cable Cars, Down of Hill is Ground Cars (its a cable cars as well, but for 40_50 people by cable). For tickets, its a separated tickets of 2 entry (entry of great wall and entry of cable-ground cars) you can purchase directly in the ticket offices, so no need to book in advance (like KLook, its very difficult to exchange the e-confirmation to physical ticket, nobody speaks english). For cable cars, it could suspend when there is windy (not stable journey of cars). Great wall is pretty amazing as you already know. But there are many winds as well, so if temparature is low, you should bring extra clothes. There are almost no restaurant out of cable stations, prepare some food and drinks. For my experience, it is very crowded in the morning till noon (many local tourist comes by group with big buses), so it could be smart if you visit it after 1pm. Indeed, its not as complicated as Beijing tourist points where you have to book.
Amazing to visit one of the great wonders of the world. Unfortunately, it rained and was packed because of the Labour Day holidays, but it was a memorable experience nonetheless.

Words can't describe the feeling I had when I went here. I was truly besides myself. The Great Wall of China was always a childhood dream of mine to visit and till this day, I can't believe I came here. Personal feelings aside, its totally worth coming. And between us, you can go beyond the perimeters and go to the "Wild Great Wall" but that's a hint for you to figure out. I will say I came here in the very beginning of 2020 and came SUPER early. I was one of the first people there and THANK GOD. Because despite it being cold as can be, many people and school children came out. I highly recommend coming super early, spend some time and leave a little after the crowds have settled in. Regardless though, its truly amazing. I will also say, prepared to get in some cardio because some of the incline can be STEEP and there's lots of walking to do. Absolutely recommend coming here whether its touristic or not. PROS: -Amazing, surreal -The scale and history is wild -There is a train from Beijing that can get you to Baldaling very fast CONS: -Can get SUPER crowded so if you can't handle crowds, be prepared. Chinese crowds are DIFFERENT. -If you're not physically fit, you may have a difficult time and may not be so fun for you

The most famous and picturesque from the accessible sections of the Great Wall. Located 70km from the city center. You should either rent a car for the whole day to take you there and back or use subway+bus. I opted for the latter (subway to Line 10 Jiandemen Station+700m walk+No.919 bus+Badaling Tourist bus - 2 hours in total). I visited the south section first, walked all the way back and then all the way to the top of the north section. My intention was to return with the cable car but unfortunately it was closed. I also noticed people walking down to the east but had no time to follow. Prepare for steep climbing, slippery floor and many steps. The handrails are relatively low and the steep sections slow moving. Proper shoes and light load are highly recommended!

Hmm... The so called must visit places in your life, there is a Chinese saying you can't be called a man unless you have visited the great wall of china. But the experience for me is just meh, first you need to book a car or tax or van to the places, the public transport to the places is always full. The journey is quite far away. And when you reach there, it is full of people, from the bottom to the top, it is like everybody squeezing in the great wall. The good thing is they already do maintenance on it so it is not that steep compared to the great wall on the other side Maybe it has too many people, so you can see a lot of spitting and littering which is not a pleasant experience Overall, maybe just visiting one time is enough

A great part of the great Wall, it is around 1 and a half hours away from Beijing. Lots of tours you can book and all very cheap, we got an English speaking tour guide along with transportation and lunch for 150 Yuen. We went during winter and it was cold and started to snow as we climbed further up the mountain! A great place to visit and a must travel destination!!!
Very crowded with tourists, lots of shop & restaurants! Careful when you walk on the walk especially for kids and elders as some are very stepping and slippery. More like a touristy check-point!

Make sure to book your ticket earlier a day or two before. Come early in the morning Open 8am until 430pm everyday. Crowded on weekends, better go on weekedays. Use train to reach the badaling train station. Be mentally prepare to climb and bring umbrella in got small child.

I reached at 6:30 AM via Didi taxi and got back to Beijing city by train. I took a cable car to North 7th and walked to North 8th, which is the highest point of the Badaling Great Wall. The view was stunning, and I wondered how our elders built the wall on the mountain and made it so long.

Probably the most well preserved part of the Great Wall, for this reason it is also the busiest part to visit - breath taking views all around. Compared to other sections of the Great Wall is also very easy to walk but does have some steep inclines/declines - other part of the wall are worth visit ahead of this but this is certainly one of the easiest parts to get to without having to hire a car
Convenient to visit from Beijing. Spectacular view. Only drawback is queue is very long in order to take cable car and it’s very crowded.

Easiest to get to, most visited and crowded section of the Great Wall outside Beijing. You can take a cheap coach bus here for less than a dollar. Recommended to get here very early (first wave), and also pay extra to take the rail up to save you some time and energy, the stairs are very steep. Also take some time to visit the lower walls where they are no people.

This is one of the buildings that you must visit when you are in Beijing, takes a while to go from Downtown(Around 80 to 90 min drive on the bus). It was already fascinating to see the building on the high way. The Badaling Great wall consist of two parts, South and North with both consist of 8 buildings each, the tour guide of the bus over exaggerated about how hard it gonna be to climb it and suggests you to take the slide car, which takes you up to the North 4 building of the Great Wall. We went up with the slide car, got to the North 8 buildings and then we walked down to the entrance and did not take the slide car down. It roughly took us 2 hours to complete it, if you have the time, it will be interesting to do both south and North. The last thing, expect lot of people!

Amazing place, but can get VERY crowded around holidays. Be sure and take the cable car to the top. It will save you time. However, I would suggest you visit one of the other Great Wall sites other than Badaling. Badaling is VERY commercial, and because of its proximity to Beijing, there are few days when you won't have to wait in line. Unfortunately the Great Wall tours to Badaling are mostly tourist rip-offs. They take you to see a Jade exhibit (which is just a jade store) where they try and sell you jade pieces that the tour company gets a kick-back from, along with a "tea exhibit" which is just a tea store. They also take you to see the Ming Tombs which are a waste of time in my opinion, and by the time you visit all of these places they give you very little time at the Great Wall. Their tour guides also speak poor English. Most of the people on my tour said they could only understand him forty percent of the time. My recommendation would be to visit one of the other Great Wall areas, other than Badaling, and rent a car and guide for the day. It will cost a little bit more, but you'll be Much happier.

This is a must-go place while you are in Beijing. Luckily, my chinese friend drove me there. But surely you can book a tour to this section of the Great wall. There will be a shuttle bus to transport you from the parking lot to the entrance. There are two sections, one is the northern and other is southern side. I chose the northern side. It tooks me about 2 hours to finish the whole until the 12th tower. The weather was really cold that day but the view was spectacular. It was a bit tired but surely worth it. Not just the great wall itselfe, the amazing mountains along the way back to Beijing was so beautiful.

I was a great experience. The lady at ticket counter was very helpful. Good thing is they accept cash. They will need passport for verification. When I went, it was cloudy and very cold. I had to buy pullover from nearby shop. Due to cloudy ⛅ weather visibility was not good after reaching top. Overall good experience. Make sure to carry water and some food. You will definitely need those.

Badaling is a one place that tourists can observe and climb the Great Wall of China. The Great Wall is a historical important place in China and popular among the local and foreign tourists. Usually crowded. Rest room facilities are available in many places along the Great Wall. Entrance ticket need to be purchased. Shoes with Rubber soles are advised as the footpath on the wall is slippery.

Good views of the Great Wall of China, but expect a lot of people. Queue for almost 2 hours to enter the cable car up the Badaling. However, it is worth the ride as it brings you all to way to the top of the Great Wall. Pre booking is absolutely necessary.

I’m staying in Beijing Central and hotel just near to Metro/Subway station. Take a High Speed Train from Beijing North Railway Station to Badaling Great Wall costs me 96CNY 1st class return ticket. Great Wall entrance fee cost me 40CNY at site counter. Another option is Cable car with entrance fee 100CNY one way or 140CNY return . All payments with AliPay apps. Alternately, can go to Badaling Great Walk by taxi with DiDi apps( like Grab or Uber ) and the cost around 250-350CNY one way.

Took the bus 877 from the Jishuan station, very easy access and the last bus leaves from the wall at 17h, leaving enough time to explore! The easy access translates into a very crowded segment of the wall.. Nevertheless, worth the visit! Very steep, do not recommend for people with trolleys ou low mobility..

Visited great wall at badaling in may. Thankfully it was not sunny and had pleasant hike. So the entrance and exit are kind of in the middle, one can either decide to visit towers on the left or on the right. There are 7 on the left and 9 to the right. It is better to visit during spring because of the climate and scenic views from top. Lovelier when cloudy. We took subway on line 13 and reached hyoying station. There are clear indications in english about where to take s2 express to reach badaling. The train frequency is pretty less so plan accordingly. The fare however is quite cheap 7rmb one way to badaling. Cab drivers might flock you and they charge 600rmb round trip but its not advisable to use cabs. The ticket to great wall is 40rmb per person, pretty reasonable. There are surprisingly clean and well equipped washrooms at the base and one on each side once on the wall. The slopes are steep in some parts. But not a difficult climb. One can accompany kids and elders in the family to badaling great wall. There are plenty of food options. So even if you are vegetarian be rest assured. There are subway and kfc outlets as also chinese restaurants in tow. All and all wonderful experience.

A must if you are in Beijing area! Yes the wall can get crowded because it is a major tourist attraction. But you can't come to China and not visit one of the worlds greatest wonders. You can climb all the way the hard way or take the lift and save time and energy. Either way its a nice experience. Steps are uneven can be tricky at times so be careful. Check it out!
Perfect place for visiting the Great Wall of China. It is about one hour by bus from Beijing. A little bit crowdy, but still the view is amazing.

From the actual Great Wall, you have the option to go left or right. The left side eventually becomes a dead end that's inaccessible at the end. Then you can continue to the right that will eventually loop down near the entrance. Extremely crowded near the beginning but thins out as you walk further. Extremely steep stairs! Prepare your passport and a form of payment such as AliPay or WeChat Pay. Short video to get an idea of what to expect starting at 6:52 - 9:02. https://youtu.be/hZ9MHLyjuoQ

Visiting and climbing The Great Wall is definitely a MUST DO on anyone's bucket list. Badaling's section of the wall is probably the most visited. The climb is challenging, the views and vistas are breathtaking. Go when the weather is cooler, like late spring, early summer.

One of the most breath taking views I have seen in my whole life. It takes a while to climb the stairs so take as many stops as needed to make it, trust me it is definitely worth it. There are love locks all over the top portion of the Badaling site where lovers profess their love to each other for eternity. One of the few things on earth that can be seen from space and in certain spots, instead of mortar they used sticky rice and even the bodies of workers that had died building the wall. Check off an item from the old bucket list....

We got there early in the morning at 8. It was well organized, but still pretty crowded. From the top station I would recommend going straight downhill on the wall and not up to the nearby high point of the wall. It gets way less crowded the further you go downhill. And I wouldnt go there around noon. When we left there were long links.

The Great Wall of Badaling in Beijing is one of the best preserved part of the Great Wall. Tourists visiting the Great Wall can choose two tracks to follow, one side of the wall is steep, while the other has a gentle slope. The gentle slope is most popular with tourists visiting the Great Wall. Take plenty of pictures and remember to carry bottled water. While on the wall, there are no toilets nearby until you reach the restaurants at the foot of the wall. Therefore make prior preparations before you climb the wall

We came in December and it was very cold and windy. Please be prepared with winter coats and accessories. Parts of the wall are very steep slopes with handrails. Others are steep stairs that vary in height but again, there are handrails. There are also flatter sections as well. If you plan to walk or see a large section of the wall, make sure you have comfortable shoes that won't slip. If you're properly prepared for the physicality of hiking the wall, it will be the most amazing experience with breathtaking views.

Bucket list stuff right here people. This is the closest portion of the Great Wall to Beijing. And so, loading up on buses on the north side of the city and able to see/wall on the wall for nearly as long as you'd like. Of course, somewhat ruined by all the people, souvenirs and winter weather make it hard to walk if iced. Truly a wonder of the world.

The great Wall of China is different from the city wall, you can't cycle here. The reason is simple it is build on hills. There is area very steep to climb, while certain area are flat. Suggest to take the North cable car as it is more tower to visit, take the south pulled train if you want the place for your own(less crowded). Ensure you will get view from both side, as it is beautiful from either side. The section open to public is well maintained. You need to get here early, as the train is always full, both way. You might be standing in the train to bada ling, S2 line.

Loved it, even though it was crowded due to Chinese New Year 🐷. Amazing to see all the work that was put into this wall and to be walking on history! Great exercise as well, Make sure to bring your walking shoes, comfortable clothes, water and of course camera!
One of the 7 wonders of the world. It’s a must place to visit and only downside is that you don’t come during their school holidays or their festivals. If not jam packed with 100k of people.

Absolutely the best place to visit the wall. Amazing structure brilliant scenery in the mountains. Take the subway there and back just be careful of the S2 trains as they are not very frequent and then your quite far from the subway stations.

It’s a great place if you like climbing steep stairs up and down and looking for that picturesque photo, the views are really great but you’re gonna darn it! It’s not a place to come if you are looking to “walk” on the Great Wall.. I recommend going to the east entrance where you can take the sky lift up and the cart slide down! Plus you can walk for miles on it. Hope this helps.
There's a High speed rail station at it's base. Recommend buying wall tickets before visiting. Restaurants are located around the cableway station. Recommended

Yes, this is a tourist trap, yes, there are a huge number of gift shops, and yes, it is crowded. Still a must see in addition to other wall locations. Amazing history and very open about the impact on the people who built the wall. Can walk the hill or take a tram to the top.

Beautiful in early April. Snow slightly. Cherry blossom. Bit crowded as it is known to be, but the renovated path is good for older slow walkers. Not as rustic yet beautiful and cooling. It's cheap and easy to get there yourself by public transport.

This is the stuff of legends. Its so hyped up, so I'm really happy to say it absolutely exceeded my expectations. Almost always extremely crowded. Some sections can be a little tough to climb. They sell water along the wall but its quite expensive. There's a few restrooms set up and trash cans. Please carry out your own trash if you can, and urinate only in the restrooms to help maintain this historic location. Amazing views along the way, and there's a spot to buy some pretty good fried chicken too! If you can brave the crowds, enjoy history, and walking in nature, I cannot recommend this enough. If you're traveling to Beijing you've gotta visit the Great Wall
A great architecture from over two thousand years ago. Amazing! The most convenient way to get here is by high-speed railway.

I visited Great Wall of Badaling in 2017 and it became a mandatory destination when you travel to China. Badaling is the site of the most visited section of the Great Wall of China, approximately 80 kilometers (50 mi) northwest of Beijing's city center, in Yanqing District (within Beijing municipality). The portion of the wall running through the site was built in 1504 during the Ming Dinasty, along with a military outpost reflecting the location's strategic importance. The highest point of Badaling is Beibalou (北八樓), approximately 1,015 meters (3,330 ft) above sea level. This is a very impressive place, taking in fresh air and enjoying the mountains scenery 👍👍👍.
My first and only visit to Great Wall. I visited in 2008. Short drive north of Beijing. Clean and superb views. It was a great experience. Highly recommended.
Bucket list place. Way too crowded even during low season in winter. Some parts were under renovation so that’s unfortunate. Too many people and kids, wouldn’t go back.

No Great Wall no hero. 2 directions, south and north. You can go up by walking or cables. It's convinient for kids and elders. There are Great Wall museum and 4D theater and they are good to see. What you need is patient for lining up. Besides, there is a museum nearby to memorize Jeme Tien Yow who is the pioneer of China railway system.

Awesome place to see the wall. I went at night and there were spectacular light shows, exhibitions, nice restaurants near the entrance. I hiked up to 4th level on North side, was really challenging but great experience. Amazed on how such a big thing can be constructed many centuries ago ans still standing strong and majestic. Ho liao oh CHina.

Badaling Great Wall is easily accessible and has easy walking conditions. It is the earliest Ming Great Wall opening to tourists, and attracts the most famous people. It fits for all visitors (wheelchair- friendly).

Badaling Great Wall (八達嶺長城) is famous for being a part of the Great Wall of China and is the most visited section. This portion of the wall was built in 1504 during the Ming Dynasty (明朝). If you visit Beijing, then it is a must that one should see the magnificence of this portion of the great wall. The Great Wall of China is one of the seven wonders of the world and the only structure that supposedly can be seen in the outer space.

For some reason I couldn't complete the preparation i should have taken to travel China as english speaker. So it was hard to arrange the trip to bedaling by bus. Finally we reached there without any problems. Once we arrived there we were great full to God for giving me the opportunity to witness of the hard work of han hand. I did climb some very steep part which required physical fitness.
Great experience. Do not buy the lift ticket (100 CNY) Wall directly to the gate and purchase the entrance only to walk on your own (20 CNY). Big tourist trap
Very nice overview to Great Wall here. You can see and walk on it for a while. Autumn + great Wall view = beautiful combination.
I took the train (line S2) and it was surprisingly easy and cheap. The views are amazing and yo can walk for miles along the wall. Amazing experience.

This was an awesome experience. How can you get close to the great wall and not go. We went mid week and it was busy. I was told weekends and summer are packed. Be prepared to walk up steep inclines--I was not. 😀
Nice spot to photo and many cute souvenirs, but care of the price okay.. btw the view ao amazing, crowded of people maybe cos i came at public holiday, but its really worth it

The day we went was during the middle of summer vacation here. It was CRAZY busy. We took the train out which was really inexpensive! We took the 887 bus back which only took 45 mins. We didn't have a guide which caused us to miss the bobsled down. If there's a way you can get a local to purchase your tickets up the cable car, you will save over $10/ticket. We did the long loop through Tower 12 which took us about 90 mins. It is a hard hike but gets you out of the crowds. This area of the wall has been completely reconstructed. You don't get to see really any crumbling walls.

The reason for the low rating was especially the bad logistics organization at the Great Wall. We made the visit on a weekday because on the weekends it is more crowded. We first tried going there with the train S2 but when we arrived at the station all tickets were sold out and the counter was closed. We then decided to take the bus 919. After driving one hour we got caught in a traffic jam and stuck there for another hour and half. The last 5 km we decided to walk. Arriving at the Great Wall there where no problems. There was quite busy but you could walk easily. We went south and north. Maybe the south way was better because not so crowded. After finishing the visit we went back to the bus station where a large crowd of people were already waiting. Because they sell you the tickets when you entering the bus and not later, it took 5-7 minutes to people got into the bus and the bus departed. After waiting almost 2 hours in a line some decided to skip the line so you can imagine there reaction of the people. At 9 pm we caught one of the last busses and after one and half hour drive we arrived in Beijing. And all this on a not very crowded day. Because it is the Great Wall we would still go again there but we would choose another location for visiting and not Badaling.
Nice section of the Wall with funicular access. Words can't express how incredible it was to be on The Great Wall of China.

Greatwall badaling is the another side from mutianyu’s greatwall gate. This gate very quiet than the others gates. It just only chinese local tourist who visited in here. So many international tourist choosed mutianyu. I will prefer to this gate because so quite than the other. The view are good and it has a train cable car like the photo who already uploaded in here. Round Trip using this cable car around 180RMB the view from cable car so nice

Must visit when you are in Beijing. if you are willing to spend the money (around 180 rmb or 26 usd), i recommend you take the pull cart to reach south tower number 5 where there are far less people and you can take your time taking photos

Do come early in the morning when tourists are not getting your way. Go to Southern Great Wall first(4 watchtowers) then come back down for Northern Great Wall (7 watchtowers, 6th was blocked so that 7th was bypassed) ). A good pair of walking shoe with strong rubber grip is needed to climb those slippery stone steps. Recommend you pack your own breakfast or lunch and have a pinic here. If you can finish your greatwall visit by 1 pm, maybe you can take a (public bus stop outside the gate) trip about an hour long ride to the end of the bus terminal and visit that Emperor Tomb 40 yuan. From this bus station take the bus back to Beijing city(subway station nearby)
One of the most beautiful Heritage of human around the world is great wall of China. It is very beautiful with colorful trees in autumn. Don't miss it if u go to china
It is an unforgettable experience walking the Great Wall of China. Although there are a lot of people at the beginning, you can hike the wall for half an hour and there will be room to spread out.
Loved it, did a private tour, highly recommend. Super efficient from Daxing. Go early morning to avoid any crowds.
The climb is not easy one would think of. Go slow from the start as I went too fast up initially and had trembling feet soon after reaching the next point.

Badaling (八达岭) is perhaps the most well-maintained section of the Great Wall of China. There are frequent buses to and from Beijing. As with all places in China, it's important to keep the passport handy. There may be some chaotic lineups and people barging to the front of ticket counters, but it's not necessary to hire tour guides.

Breathtaking. We could have easily looked at the forecast, saw the 9°F temperature and said... Let's pass, but I'm so glad we didn't. Words and pictures can't even describe the vastness of the Great Wall. Seeing my 5y/o son scale the extremely steep steps with confidence was awesome.
Mao President of China once said: “If you never been at The Great Wall, you are not a superior men”. It is a must-see if you come to Beijing. Don’t miss!
My 4th trip to the Wall, first trip to Badaling. Always amazing and the weather was perhaps the best I have ever experienced in Beijing.
Must visit at least once in a lifetime. Cable car is available nowadays. So convenient.

went here when the weather wasn't really good. foggy, windy and a little bit cold. I went there by tour bus. but my friend once went to badaling by train and she said its quite cheap. some people told me than mutianyu is better than badaling.
So amazing Great Wall, biggest one from 7 Great Walls, totally 16 towers! We climbed less than 4 hours, great experience!
For local people need book advance tickets.. For Foreigner, your can't book advance tickets, just go to counter and buy when you to go in..
Visited here during winter and it can get suupercold. Nice that’s it very much less people but the cold was crazy, so be prepared if you’re coming during winter.

Went in the winter. Less crowded for sure! I did prepare well for the cold. Luckily, it was a sunny day and not very windy. There were no foliage in the surrounding mountains but the scenery is still amazingly beautiful.

We hire a taxi for a full day to go to a less crowded section of the wall, we were the only Occidentals on the area, this is simply espectacular, no words can described the beauty and size of this marvel of the Chinese ingenuity.
The “expectation vs reality” meme about Great Wall is real ! It’s still so worth it . Be generous with the sun block . Looks cloudy but tans the hell out of you !.. Dress appropriately for the hike !

This was an exhilarating experience! Please don't attempt unless you are physically fit enough and aren't afraid of heights.... Do not underestimate how steep it is and at times the air can be really dry... Other than the obvious this is an amazing opportunity and the history behind it makes it worth the climb! Oh and you get a really cool trinket (not free) a gold medallion for making it up...they will engrave your name and date on it... there's also a souvenir book and photo to document the climb At the wall there are lots of souvenir shops, cafes and a buffet..

Was a nice experience seeing and climbing this ancient masterpiece. It is advisable going there via the daily buses going there between 9am to 12.30pm instead of using a taxi. It is quite some distance from Beijing Town. Connect to the bus stop from where you are using the subway and you board this bus no 877. And you will use it when coming back to Beijing. The wall is very extensive and when experiencing it is like a hike. Do some exercise beforehand if possible.
The magnificent views and the chain of castles are awe-inspiring. I will never forget it.

Wow. Fantastic to see the Great wall spread out on the crest of the hills on both sides of the valley,quite amazing views. Most of the wall walk includes many steps and inclined paths which may be difficult for some people. Having said that you dont have to climb the wall to see the fantastic wall sprawl out and the amazing views. Has food and drinks available after you enter after paying for a ticket. Souvenir shops and a "Great wall book" that you can purchase along with an 8 x 10cm photo of you and the wall in the background for a fair price. The book and photo is stamped and signed on the date of your visit. This section of the wall is in really good condition (helped along with a bit of maintenance).
A must visit in your lifetime. Great experience. Views are awesome. As more as you walk the more you love it.

Definitely a classic that takes you back to history. If you are physically fit I 'd highly recommend skip the gondola and climb yourself. It gets steeper on your way and can get slippery if wet. so use caution and watch your steps! Often gets quite crowded too but most people stop at the north 8th tower and turn back. Don't stop yet! keep going until you can't go any further at north 12th tower. It's much more fun and significantly less jammed, but use extreme caution as it's very steep and there is no longer hand rail. Best part is that you don't have to go all the way back - there is a shortcut near the 10th tower to get off. You 'll have to cross a weird zoo and whole bunch of shops to get back to where you came from though.

Worse experience ever! This local people jam-packed this location. The locals does not have any respect for their landmark. There is a ton of people here. The experience will make it where never want to return to this area. It does not look beautiful when there's millions of people next to you trying to take a photo of a beautiful place like this. Also the government shuts down a portion of wall, where you can explore and walk further away from everybody.

Breathtaking views as long as you check the weather beforehand. Getting here is a lot of work, so don't let possible fogs ruin your day. The first few sections are very crowded but it thins out significantly after about 10 minutes of walking. Some areas can be extremely steep and don't even have staircases (You may literally be pulling yourself up/down with the handrails), so older visitors should be aware. Wear sneakers or hiking shoes with good grip and bring water! There are no vendors in the middle of the trek! The only reason this place does not have 5 stars is because of the surprisingly inconvenient transportation options if you're going from the Beijing city area. The trains run infrequently and many of the "taxi" drivers are unofficial/private-cars. Obviously, your experience may differ dramatically if you're going as part of a tour group.
A rather touristy but very photogenic part of the Great Wall. It is very easy to get there from Beijing, about one hour by bus from Jishuitan Subway station. A perfect half day trip.
Perhaps the easily accessible and most well-preserved section of the Great Wall. You go go up by foot as well as cable car, and enjoy the wall and the scenic valley.
Fun, interesting historic site. Ride the train up from the city -- it's easy and you can choose your own time to go home.
One can see why it's one of the Wonders of the World. Wear comfy clothes and sensible shoes. Uneven steps so watch your step
Super easy to get there. If you have time; go to thiamin square and take the public bus for 20RMB.
Best spot is at 9post!!!!! But the course a bit hard from post 8-11..just be careful ^^

Amazing scenery ! Majestic Great Wall of China! The whole area is simply beautiful. But it is swamped by thousands of noisy and loud Chinese domestic tourists. The ambiance is ruined. 2 hrs queue up and down. 4 hours wasted. Go to other sections of the Great Wall if you want some quiet moments to appreciate and take in the history of the Great Wall.

This is the most visited section of the great wall.. the wall is so long about 8 km always crowded with group of tourists everywhere..be sure you wont get separated from your group and pay attention at time duration of your visit..use comfortable sport shoes to prepare for a long hiking..the view from the top is magnificient...
What an amazing place, must see! Bring great walking shoes and don't plan on walking when it rains.
Avoid visiting during Chinese public holidays if you don't want to get stuck for hours in a crowd that never ends. Plus mind the weather on a day of your visit - it can be very hot there.
It’s spectacular view and such an impressive site you must visit if you ever visit Beijing :)
Great world heritage site to visit half a day. Don't forget good shoes to walk on the hills 😉
Just After the Spring Festival/Chinese New year, there were only few visitors. The Air quality was at its best.

Amazing experience. I came here in December, it was sunny ☀️ and super cold + windy, but in the morning there were no people at all, so every second of that freezing cold was worth it. And the rest can't describe what you see, and the photo can't do it justice.
Finally got to tick off one of the wonders of the world on my bucket list, even managed to take the toboggan ride down! Definitely got to go once in your life!
Really for me visited this iconic place is Good experience... You can check your energy level
I am at Switzerland on Mountain & All other photos of Switzerland (Lion) & Tulip Garden -Lisse -Amsterdam

An amazing and breathtaking experience. Although some sections are very steep and can be quite difficult to climb (top tip: wear appropriate shoes), the views are well worth the hike (try to get as high as possible). It can get quite busy and crowded due to a large number of tourist groups, so keep and eye on your surroundings and make sure not to trip! It is relatively easy to navigate through the Great Wall - if you're lost, simply follow the signs or follow the crowd. There is a large variety of tourist shops, so get your negotiation skills ready. After you finish (if you climbed during summer), make sure to treat yourself with some cool ice cream as I can guarantee you'll be sweating.
One of the seven wonders in the world. You must visit when you go to china. In badaling you can use cable car for go to the top
Thankfully I had a colleague as a guide as the while operation is mad and confusing, but quite an experience. Take supplies, comfy walking shoes, and massive muscular thighs.

CLOSES AT 5, HAVE TO GET OFF THE WALL AT 4:30. -- Don't believe the signs, staff or information online it is shut by 5pm, everyone is removed from the wall at 4:30pm. The Wall closes at 5pm and the staff kick you off at 4:30pm. It's important if you're planning to visit to leave enough time before 4:30pm to see the Wall, but also to consider your travel options. If you wait until they kick you off at 4:30pm you will miss the next train back to Beijing and be forced to wait 2 hours in the station for the following one (everything else in the are also shuts at 5pm...)!
A symbol of the richness of history, a tourist must experience this place throughout his life

A very nice place. It is considered to be one of the greatest wonders of the world. When visiting, take enough water, snacks, and strong comfortable walking/hiking shoes. It is an intermediate to hard hike to the top. Unless, you take the cable cart to the top. If you are just a little fit, the hike is worth it. Phenomenal views which you will not see if you take the cable cart. Also, there's a slide down if you get worn out as you make your way down. It gets windy as you walk to the top. A jacket is recommended! Public transportation is available to reach the wall if you don't want to be limited by the time restrictions from a group tour. It takes some to maneuvering your way to the Wall in public transportation. Only cost 11 RMB from Beijing to Badaling. Take Cash. Also, book online for the tickets. Badaling is the most famous but there are other sites as well. Research before going.

The Badaling Great Wall, built during the Ming Dynasty, defended Beijing from northern invasions. Its strategic location and robust construction symbolized China's advanced engineering and commitment to national security.
Amazing historical site! We went to both Badaling and Mutianyu, and both are amazing and offer a different experience
Went there during national holiday! The number of people is just tooooooo crazyyyyyyy!!!! But it’s exciting!

Great place to visit the Great Wall. It's super easy to access by train and bus, so you definitely don't need to get a tour to come here. Apart from the ease of access the Great Wall is really just what you expect: a really great wall. Pro tip: all the Chinese tourists will take the ropeway to the top of the south side of the wall, so if you want to enjoy the wall with relatively few people around just walk to the bottom of the south side and then go up there.

Came in May month. It was raining when we came & the floor surrounding the shops were almost flooded & it was not recommended to go up to great wall as it will be very slippery. Came back on a weekend & it's hot & crowded. At the 5th station, local people would be sitting at the window opening, blocking the nice view... would recommend to take the cable car to 8th stain instead of taking the pulley to 4th station
Fantastic piece of history. Easy to access thanks to HSR Station located on site. Makes for a pleasant, but steep hike.

Visited way back in March 2010 and was blown away by the sheer scale of the Wall. In c. 220 B.C., under Qin Shi Huang, sections of earlier fortifications were joined together to form a united defence system against invasions from the north. Construction continued up to the Ming dynasty (1368–1644), when the Great Wall became the world's largest military structure. Its historic and strategic importance is matched only by its architectural significance.

The Great Wall of China is a series of fortifications made of stone, brick, tamped earth, wood, and other materials, generally built along an east-to-west line across the historical northern borders of China to protect the Chinese states and empires against the raids and invasions of the various nomadic groups.

🇨🇳 Великая Китайская стена — это не фото. Это чувство. Сегодня я стоял там, где история буквально лежит под ногами. На Великой Китайской стене. Сложно передать словами, какое это ощущение: ты идёшь по камням, которым сотни лет, и понимаешь — это не просто достопримечательность, это символ человеческой силы, характера и терпения. Стена уходит вдаль, карабкается по горам, исчезает в тумане… и ты ловишь себя на мысли, что смотришь на неё и думаешь: «Это реально построили люди… руками… без современных технологий…» Вот где масштаб. Вот где мощь. Вот где дыхание времени. И знаете, что самое крутое? Когда стоишь там наверху, становится тихо внутри. Потому что такие места не просто впечатляют — они напоминают, насколько огромен мир, и насколько важно жить ярко. 📸 Делюсь этими кадрами — пусть они сохранят этот момент. А я точно знаю: это воспоминание — на всю жизнь.
